description:
Repository configuration declares whether state-mutating commands may run inside a linked
non-primary checkout, and resolves to refusal when nothing is declared.

## Background

The configuration already carries a worktree section whose lease-enforcement key is typed,
parsed at load, and defaulted in one place. A write-policy stance follows that same shape: a
typed value with a stated default, so a repository chooses its stance in version-controlled
configuration rather than through an undeclared environment convention. The shipped default
refuses, because the adopter who never considered the question is the one the divergent-store
hazard hurts.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A typed write-policy value parses from the worktree configuration section and rejects unknown tokens at load time with a message naming the accepted ones.
- [hard] REQ-02: With no declared value, and with no worktree section at all, the resolved stance refuses state-mutating commands inside a linked non-primary checkout.
- [hard] REQ-03: A declared permissive stance resolves to permitting those commands, and the precedence between the declared stance and a per-invocation override is stated once and covered by tests.
- [hard] REQ-04: This repository declares the permissive stance in its own tracker configuration, so its linked agent checkouts keep mutating their local stores.
- [hard] REQ-05: The configuration reference states the key, its accepted values, its default, and how an absent section resolves, worded as the repository's declared stance rather than as a promise of enforcement.

## Notes

The neighbouring lease-enforcement key resolves differently depending on whether the section
is present at all. The write-policy key states its own resolution explicitly rather than
inheriting that asymmetry.
title: Worktree write policy configuration key
